title: Training-row sampling gave overlapping run-tail ranges for two PDO models fitted within 1950-2025
abstract: We tested how coefficient sampling changes model checks for the longest negative Pacific Decadal Oscillation run in a saved 1950-2025 record. We sampled training rows in 12- and 24-month blocks. For each of 499 coefficient draws per case, we simulated 999 complete records with observed ENSO held fixed. The mean fraction of maximum runs at least 72 months long was 0.0324 to 0.0326 for fits through 2019, and 0.1307 to 0.1396 for fits through 2025. With 12-month blocks, the central 95% of coefficient-specific tail estimates was 0.0040 to 0.0953 and 0.0185 to 0.3650. The ranges overlap. Both cross 0.05. Coefficient sampling did not remove the difference between average model references. It did show that a sharp threshold interpretation of one fitted tail neglects substantial sensitivity. These are descriptive model ranges, not confidence limits or proof of a regime change. One revised index, fixed ENSO, a fixed residual distribution, limited memory and simulation noise restrict inference. Original code, aggregate results, simulation evidence, source hashes, a figure and arithmetic checks are included. External source records stay outside the publication.

display.caption: Tail estimates for maximum negative runs across 499 coefficient draws per case. Central ranges overlap across fitting periods. These are model sensitivity distributions, not confidence intervals.
